transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-11
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Evan Ruiz (Redwood Platform), Maya Chen (Catalyst CTO), Liam O'Connor (Catalyst CISO), Sofia Alvarez (Platform Eng), Noah Patel (Legal)

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for joining. Quick check, does the time still work for Catalyst?
[00:05] Maya (Catalyst): Yep all good, thanks Jordan. We're mainly here to go over compliance artifacts and how we'd onboard evidence into your Trust Center and then talk RBAC/SSO and the KMS question.
[00:12] Jordan: Great. Priya from our SE team will run through the controls mapping and then Evan can cover logs and encryption flow.
[00:18] Priya (Redwood): Cool, I pulled together a high-level controls mapping. It maps Redwood's operational controls to SOC2 categories and ISO27k clauses. I will say upfront some of the field names in our docs can be a bit terse — if anything looks off call it out.
[00:30] Liam (Catalyst): When you say "Trust Center" is that the same as the compliance portal? We want programmatic access for audit automation.
[00:36] Jordan: Yes it's the Trust Center — you can download certs and artifacts, and we can grant view-only links or SSO access for your auditors. Programmatic export is limited today but we have a metadata API we can use for integration.
[00:45] Sofia (Catalyst): Programmatic is important because we want to ingest control evidence into our audit toolchain. Are there webhooks or an API?
[00:52] Evan (Redwood): Right now the Trust Center supports per-account links and a UI download, plus an API that returns evidence metadata and signed URLs for artifacts. We can add an export job to dump evidence into an S3 bucket you control as a short-term solution.
[01:05] Maya: That S3 path sounds useful. Any concerns about token expiry or signed URL lifetime?
[01:12] Evan: Signed URLs are time-limited; for bulk transfer we do a handoff job that rotates tokens and we can coordinate timing. We'll document the exact TTL in the handoff notes.
[01:22] Noah (Catalyst): From a legal perspective we need a record of who downloaded what. Does the Trust Center include audit trails for artifact access?
[01:29] Priya: Yes we capture who downloaded artifacts and we include that in audit logs. The log entries contain user email, artifact id, timestamp — though sometimes the identity mapping comes through as service accounts, so we advise using dedicated SSO accounts for auditors.
[01:42] Liam: Great. On RBAC — we have strict segregation of duties. Does Redwood support SCIM provisioning and role scoping per environment?
[01:49] Priya: We support SCIM and SAML. Our recommended pattern is to provision groups via SCIM and map them to Redwood roles. Role scoping by environment is supported through project-level RBAC and resource tags. I can send a template mapping of roles to least privilege defaults.
[02:03] Maya: Would that include admin, billing, developer, and read-only auditor roles?
[02:07] Priya: Exactly. We generally include admin, power-user, read-only, billing, and auditor. We can show sample permission matrices.
[02:15] Jordan: Also worth noting for Dedicated and Private deployments we have additional RBAC layers and custom role configs if needed.
[02:22] Sofia: For SSO, our IdP is Okta. We want provisioning via SCIM and just-in-time group sync. Any gotchas?
[02:29] Priya: Okta is our most common IdP. SCIM provisioning is straightforward but watch out for email mismatches and case sensitivity. We'll provide the attribute mappings we use.
[02:36] Liam: KMS and encryption is a sticking point. We want to use our own keys — customer-managed keys — and prefer HSM-backed keys in AWS. How flexible are you there?
[02:44] Evan: For Hosted we support AWS KMS with our managed keys by default. Customer-managed KMS is supported for Dedicated and Private options; for Hosted we can integrate customer KMS under a contract — technically doable but there are limitations on key residency and rotate/rotate policies.
[02:58] Jordan: To add, if you require HSM and per-customer key isolation we typically recommend Redwood Private or Dedicated reserved capacity. That gives you full control of the KMS integration.
[03:08] Liam: So for a proof-of-concept we could try customer-managed keys in a Dedicated preview?
[03:15] Priya: Yes, we can scope a short Dedicated pilot. We'll need to confirm hardware region and whether you require in-region HSM.
[03:23] Maya: Data residency: we need logs and keys to stay in eu-west-1. Is that feasible?
[03:28] Evan: We support region scoping. For Hosted accounts we have EU regions with data residency guarantees; Dedicated and Private give stronger contractual residency. We'll document what lives where and which artifacts are replicated.
[03:40] Sofia: Regarding audit logs, we want near real-time delivery to our Splunk stack. What's your recommended approach?
[03:46] Evan: Push-based log forwarding to your S3 -> Splunk ingestion is the usual path; we also have a streaming endpoint you can consume. We'll run a short integration test to measure latency.
[03:58] Liam: And retention? Our policy is seven years for certain artifacts, but operational logs are two years. Can retention be configured?
[04:06] Priya: Retention policies are configurable per artifact type, though longer archival storage will incur costs. We'll outline retention defaults and options.
[04:15] Maya: For the controls mapping, can we get a single spreadsheet mapping your controls to our SOC2 control statements?
[04:22] Priya: Yes that's what I built — sample mapping will be shared. It will include control owner, evidence location, and evidence frequency.
[04:30] Noah: Quick legal Q — will the Trust Center artifacts suffice for our auditors, or do we need additional attestations?
[04:36] Jordan: Typically SOC2 Type II plus the ISO readout and artifact evidence are sufficient. For bespoke requirements we can provide supplemental notes and engineer attestation.
[04:45] Liam: On the timeline, we want to close onboarding and start pilot within two weeks. Is that realistic?
[04:50] Jordan: Two weeks for initial handoff is tight but doable for a pilot — if Catalyst provides IdP metadata and sample accounts quickly. We'll prioritize the RBAC mapping and log export.
[05:00] Maya: Sounds good. Can you enumerate success criteria for the pilot?
[05:04] Priya: Sure: 1) Trust Center access for Catalyst auditors with downloadable artifacts; 2) SCIM provisioning working with Okta and role mapping; 3) Audit logs forwarded to Catalyst SIEM with acceptable latency; 4) KMS integration validated for key residency or an agreed path if Hosted can't meet HSM needs.
[05:22] Jordan: I'll summarize and send a checklist. Any last questions?
[05:28] Sofia: One small thing — are there sample legal clauses for key custody we can review?
[05:33] Noah: Yes we need to see contractual language around encryption and data residency.
[05:36] Jordan: We'll include our standard KMS appendix and show options for Dedicated/Private.
[05:42] Liam: Thanks all. Looking forward to the docs.
[05:45] Jordan: Thanks, we'll follow up with the SOC2 and RBAC artifacts.

Meeting recap (end):
- Agreed to grant Trust Center read access and share SOC2 & ISO artifacts.
- SE to send RBAC/SCIM mapping + role templates.
- Platform to coordinate audit log export pilot and provide details on signed URL TTLs.
- Open decision: customer-managed keys vs Redwood-managed keys — determine after legal review.

End of transcript.
